properties.description:

inches.

* WHERE...Northern Copper Valley, including the eastern Denali

roads.

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key 20 to 60 NM out
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 18 at 8:39AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key out 60 nm...

At 839 AM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists detected a
strong thunderstorm, capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots.
This thunderstorm was located 11 nm north of Floyd's Wall Northeast,
moving south at 15 knots.

Locations that will be affected include...
Floyd's Wall Northeast.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM NORTH OF FLOYDS WALL

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Eastern Chichagof Island; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 18 at 4:34AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continue through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and
spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain
will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat,
Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36
hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and
lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including
Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time
frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For
context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are
not historically extreme.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN EXPECTED MONDAY NIGHT THROUGH TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Upper Hood River Valley
properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 18 at 5:27AM PDT until October 18 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 33F to 36F under mostly clear skies
will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...Upper Hood River Valley.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM PDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants, or
temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

NWSheadline: FROST ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM PDT THIS MORNING
